hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated oxidising agent does to a C=C bond compared with cold, dilute conditions.
Look at the substitution of the C=C bonds in retinol, most carbons have one H and one carbon group, while some have two carbon groups and no H.
Remember that any aldehyde first formed is easily oxidised further under vigorous heating, so think about what survives at the end.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two different KMnO4 conditions**

Cold, dilute acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives mild oxidation to a diol. It does not break the carbon chain.

Hot, concentrated acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives vigorous oxidative cleavage. It breaks the $\text{C=C}$ bond completely.

**Apply the cleavage rules to the fragments**

When a $\text{C=C}$ is broken, each C becomes a $\text{C=O}$ group. Use this pattern:
$$\text{R-CH=} \rightarrow \text{R-CHO} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O (a ketone)}$$
So a $\text{=CH-}$ group gives an aldehyde first, and a $\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)-}$ group gives a ketone.

**Allow for further oxidation under hot conditions**

Ketones resist further oxidation, but aldehydes do not. Under hot, concentrated conditions any aldehyde is oxidised straight on to a carboxylic acid:
$$\text{R-CHO + [O]} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH}$$

**Conclude for retinol**

Retinol contains several $\text{-CH=CH-}$ and $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)=CH-}$ units plus a primary alcohol $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ which is also oxidised to $-\text{COOH}$. To break all the $\text{C=C}$ bonds and fully oxidise the fragments we need hot, concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4$. The surviving final products are ketones and carboxylic acids, with no aldehydes left.

options.A: Cold, dilute KMnO4 gives syn-diols, not cleavage of the C=C skeleton. Also aldehydes would not survive as final products under cleavage conditions, they are oxidised further.
options.B: The product pair ketones and carboxylic acids is correct for vigorous cleavage, but cold, dilute conditions are wrong. Cold, dilute does not break C=C bonds.
options.C: Hot, concentrated conditions are correct for breaking C=C bonds, but aldehydes cannot be final products. Under hot, concentrated oxidation any $\text{R-CHO}$ formed from $\text{=CH-}$ is further oxidised to $\text{R-COOH}$.
options.D: Hot, concentrated acidified KMnO4 cleaves every C=C in retinol. Fragments of type $\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)-}$ give ketones which resist further oxidation, fragments of type $\text{=CH-}$ give aldehydes which are oxidised on to carboxylic acids, and the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ gives a carboxylic acid. Final mixture contains ketones and carboxylic acids.
